Topic: The Logic of Abstract Vector Spaces

Target audience: University students (Undergraduate level)

Section: section_1 — From Concrete to Abstract: The Intuition

Lecture lines:
Vectors are more than just arrows.
Think of waves or polynomials.
Objects sharing common logical rules.

Planned animations:
1. Fade in a set of discrete physical objects (colored #FFD700 circles).
2. Morph circles into abstract nodes (#00CED1 dots) connected by lines.
3. Highlight the abstraction path with a glowing arrow (#FFFFFF).

Section: section_2 — The Rulebook: The 8 Axioms

Lecture lines:
Eight axioms define the game.
Space-Bot strictly obeys these rules.
Violations trigger a logical error.

Planned animations:
1. Display a stack of 8 abstract rule cards (#4682B4).
2. Flash each card individually as a defining principle.
3. Stack cards into a single block with a central title.

Section: section_3 — Example: The Polynomial Vector Space

Lecture lines:
Polynomials form a vector space.
Adding polynomials adds their DNA.
Scaling stretches the polynomial curve.

Planned animations:
1. Show a polynomial p(x) = ax^2 + bx + c (#FF4500).
2. Break coefficients into distinct basis component vectors (#32CD32).
3. Display these vectors spanning a 3D coordinate volume.

Section: section_4 — Application: The Geometry of Data

Lecture lines:
Data lives in feature spaces.
Emojis act as coordinate vectors.
Adding moods creates new feelings.

Planned animations:
1. Display a cloud of data points (#8A2BE2).
2. Show a line of best fit emerging through the cloud (#FFFFFF).
3. Highlight the orthogonal projection lines from points to the fit.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Conclusion

Lecture lines:
Abstract spaces unify diverse systems.
Structure powers AI and physics.
Logic is the universal language.

Planned animations:
1. Recap the abstraction step (#FFD700 -> #00CED1).
2. Re-show the axiom block (#4682B4).
3. Fade out everything to black background (#000000).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Application: The Geometry of Data", [

            "Emojis act as coordinate vectors.",
            "Adding moods creates new feelings."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a cloud of data points (#8A2BE2)
        data_points = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#8A2BE2") for _ in range(20)])
        for p in data_points:

                np.random.uniform(-1.5, 2.0),
                0

        self.play(FadeIn(data_points))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#8A2BE2")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a line of best fit emerging through the cloud (#FFFFFF)
        line = Line(start=np.array([1.5, -0.5, 0]), end=np.array([6.5, 1.5, 0]), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the orthogonal projection lines from points to the fit
        projections = VGroup()
        for p in data_points:
            # Simple projection point on line
            t = np.dot(p.get_center() - line.get_start(), line.get_vector()) / np.dot(line.get_vector(), line.get_vector())
            proj = line.get_start() + np.clip(t, 0, 1) * line.get_vector()
            projections.add(Line(p.get_center(), proj, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2))
        
        self.play(Create(projections))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Rulebook: The 8 Axioms", ["Eight axioms define the game.", "Space-Bot strictly obeys these rules.", "Violations trigger a logical error."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE_C)
        
        # Use Group instead of VGroup to support ImageMobject
        axiom_cards = Group()
        for i in range(8):
            card = ImageMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/card.png")
            # Anchor to grid B4 through E6 (columns 4-6, rows B-E)
            row = i // 2 + 1 # 1-4 mapped to B-E
            col = i % 2 + 4  # 4-5
            self.place_at_grid(card, f"{'BCDE'[i//2]}{col}", scale_factor=0.3)
            axiom_cards.add(card)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(axiom_cards))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN_C)
        
        # Flash animation
        for card in axiom_cards:
            self.play(Indicate(card, color=GREEN_B), run_time=0.2)
        
        # Create central stack using Group (since VGroup strictly requires VMobject)
        stack = Group(*[ImageMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/card.png") for _ in range(8)])
        stack.arrange(DOWN, buff=-0.5).scale(0.3)
        stack_title = Text("The 8 Rules", font_size=20, color=WHITE).scale(0.75)
        
        # Use Group for container as well to avoid VGroup type error with raster images
        rule_book = Group(stack, stack_title).arrange(DOWN)
        
        # Place in area (B4-B5)
        self.place_in_area(rule_book, 'B4', 'B5', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(axiom_cards, rule_book))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED_C)
        
        error_sign = Text("ERROR!", font_size=32, color=RED, weight=BOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(error_sign, 'C6', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(error_sign, scale=0.5))
        self.play(Indicate(rule_book))
        self.wait(2)

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
